title: An ordinary henselization at a prime is ind-etale over the original ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal, and let $H$ be an ordinary henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the canonical composite $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), property (2), applied to A_p; the extension to A uses the filtered principal-localization presentation of A_p and ind-etale composition. The universal-property convention is Tag 04GQ (definition-henselization).

proof.text: Set $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak p$ is prime, $1\in S$ and $s,t\in S$ imply $st\in S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations] with $P=A$: $R$ is the filtered colimit of $A_s$, indexed by the small divisibility preorder on $S$, with its canonical structural map from $A$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] to the identity etale map $A\to A$ to see that $A\to A_s$ is etale, and then clause (1), now to $A\to A_s$, to see that each $A_s$ has finite presentation. Thus $A\to R$ is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

Put $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$ and $k=R/\mathfrak m$. The ring $R$ is local: a fraction $a/s$ outside $\mathfrak pR$ has $a\notin\mathfrak p$, and then $s/a$ is its inverse; $\mathfrak pR$ is proper since a prime contains no denominator in $S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] to $(R,\mathfrak m)$. Its category of etale $R$-algebras $B$ with $k\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\mathfrak mB$ is essentially small and filtered; take a small skeleton for the stated colimit and denote the diagram by $(B_i)$ and its colimit coprojections by $\iota_i:B_i\to C$. This gives an $R$-algebra structure $\eta_C:R\to C$, a henselian pair $(C,J)$ with $J=\mathfrak mC$, and an induced isomorphism $e_C:k\xrightarrow{\sim}C/J$. Each $B_i$ has finite presentation by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization].

source.place: Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization), construction of the filtered etale colimit and its quotient; algebra.tex Tag 00U1 for finite presentation

proof.text: The henselian pair from Step 2 is local by a direct use of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. For $z\in J$, the finite cyclic $C$-algebra $D=C/(1-z)$ has $JD=D$, so $D/JD=0$. Its sole idempotent has both $0$ and $1$ of $D$ as lifts; uniqueness gives $D=0$, so $1-z$ is a unit of $C$. If $x\notin J$, the field $C/J\cong k$ supplies $y\in C$ with $1-xy\in J$, so $xy$ and hence $x$ are units. Thus $C$ is local with maximal ideal $J$ and is henselian local because $(C,J)$ is henselian. The structural residue-field isomorphism $e_C:k\to C/J$ also gives $\eta_C^{-1}(J)=\mathfrak m$, so $\eta_C$ is local.

source.place: Tag 09XE (definition-henselian-pair) and Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), idempotent-lifting characterization; the locality argument is written out

proof.text: Write $\eta_H:R\to H$ for the given local map. By [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], $H$ is henselian local. Put $k_C=C/\mathfrak m_C=C/J$. Its local structure map induces $e_H:k\to k_H=H/\mathfrak m_H$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base $R$, source algebra $C$, target $H$, prime $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_C$, and residue map $\tau=e_H\circ e_C^{-1}:k_C\to k_H$. Locality of $\eta_C$ and $\eta_H$ gives contraction $\mathfrak m$ on both sides, and $\tau$ is a $k$-algebra map. The lemma gives a local $R$-algebra map $f:C\to H$. Apply the defining universal property of $H$, with henselian local target $C$ and local map $\eta_C$, to obtain a local $R$-algebra map $g:H\to C$. Thus $f\eta_C=\eta_H$ and $g\eta_H=\eta_C$.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit); the universal property in the cited definition

proof.text: Both $g\circ f$ and $\mathrm{id}_C$ are local $R$-algebra endomorphisms of $C$. On residue fields, $(\overline g\circ\overline f)\circ e_C=e_C$, since both maps are over $R$; cancel the isomorphism $e_C$ to get $\overline g\circ\overline f=\mathrm{id}_{k_C}$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit], now with source and henselian target $C$, prime $\mathfrak m_C$ and residue map $\mathrm{id}_{k_C}$, gives $g\circ f=\mathrm{id}_C$. Both $f\circ g$ and $\mathrm{id}_H$ are local maps satisfying $h\eta_H=\eta_H$, so the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], with target $H$, gives $f\circ g=\mathrm{id}_H$. Hence $f$ and $g$ are inverse $R$-algebra isomorphisms. This does not assume in advance that $H$ has residue field $k$.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), uniqueness, and the defining universal property

proof.text: Use the same small filtered diagram $(B_i)$ and replace its colimit coprojections by $j_i=f\circ\iota_i:B_i\to H$. These form a cocone since $f$ is an $R$-algebra map. To verify the colimit property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], take any compatible $R$-algebra cocone $\mu_i:B_i\to T$. The original colimit gives a unique $u:C\to T$ with $u\iota_i=\mu_i$. This $u$ respects $R$: choose any stage $i$ (the index category is nonempty) with structural map $\eta_i:R\to B_i$; then $u\eta_C=u\iota_i\eta_i=\mu_i\eta_i=\eta_T$. Then $u\circ g:H\to T$ satisfies $(u\circ g)j_i=u\iota_i=\mu_i$. Conversely, if $v:H\to T$ has $vj_i=\mu_i$, uniqueness for $C$ gives $v\circ f=u$, whence $v=u\circ g$. Thus $H$, with its given structural map $\eta_H=f\eta_C$, is a filtered colimit of the same etale finitely presented $R$-algebras. By [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], $R\to H$ is ind-etale.

source.place: Tag 002F, colimit universal property; elementary verification of the transported cocone

proof.text: Steps 1 and 6 give ind-etale maps $A\to R$ and $R\to H$ for the specified structural maps. Apply the composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] to conclude that the canonical composite $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ is ind-etale. No argument or cited statement required Noetherianity.
